label: PF Backlog 593
title: EDP-12: Generated-product residency manifest (data_classes/home_region/allowed_regions/backup/kms/egress/retention) + build/deploy gate
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

decisions.note: Gate 1 embeds Gate 1.5 sha c62d9e5ac577: 16 findings, 0 pending (2 accepted: shared Go types, fleet metrics; both with why/revisit). Explicit home_region, IN template, warn-first, profile bounds.
Gate 1 embeds Gate 1.5 sha ac10db32605a: 14 findings, 0 pending (4 accepted/scoped: Python pre-check, gate events, JSON schema, alerting). Explicit IN home, profile bounds, warn-first, fail-closed.

brief.problem: No record or enforcement of where generated product data resides; US was proposed as a silent default.
brief.what_adds: Explicit home_region (IN template) + residency manifest + fail-closed build/deploy gate with stable codes and warn-first rollout.
brief.why: Enterprise compliance requires data-class and region guarantees; India-first deployments must not be silently homed in the US.
brief.who_feels: Enterprise customers, compliance reviewers, India-first operators
brief.success: A product declares home_region (IN in the template); the gate rejects missing/unknown home, out-of-region backup/KMS/egress, and bad retention with stable codes.

objective: Emit a per-product residency manifest (explicit home_region; IN template) with data_classes/allowed_regions/backup/kms/egress/retention and enforce it with a Go build/deploy validator against counsel-owned profiles: warn for the first release, then block; unknown/missing home always blocks.
acceptance_criteria: core/packaging.build emits a residency section with all six groups populated: data_classes (non-empty), home_region (REQUIRED; no silent default), allowed_regions (non-empty, includes home_region), backup {regions, encrypted=true, frequency}, kms {provider, region, rotation_days>0}, egress {allowed_regions, subprocessors}, retention {days, legal_hold}; core.packaging.validate rejects a manifest with missing/unknown home_region or an invalid residency section.

A Go module go/residencymanifest (Manifest/Policy/Validate) + cmd/pfresidency validates a manifest against config/residency-profiles/<home>.json: unknown/missing home -> fail closed; home in allowed_regions; backup/kms/egress regions subset of allowed_regions; retention.days > 0 and <= policy.retention_days when set; recognized backup.frequency; all six groups; block/warn mode; JSON report with stable error codes (RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME, RESIDENCY_HOME_NOT_ALLOWED, RESIDENCY_BACKUP_REGION, RESIDENCY_KMS_REGION, RESIDENCY_EGRESS_REGION, RESIDENCY_RETENTION, RESIDENCY_MISSING_GROUP, RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_FREQUENCY).

scripts/dev/residency_gate.py builds/loads the packaging manifest from config/residency-manifest.json (template) or products/<project>/residency-manifest.json (override), invokes the Go validator, and blocks (exit 1) or warns per config/residency-policy.json gate_mode; --report is non-fatal; warn mode prints a one-line stderr summary.

Tests cover the Go validator (valid, unknown region, missing home, home not allowed, backup/kms/egress outside allowed, zero/over retention, invalid backup/KMS fields, missing groups), the Python manifest/gate (six groups, validate rejects missing, IN template, override precedence, block/warn exit codes, warn stderr), language_rule_review, and precheck (45+ gates).

5. Policy bounds + conformance + ownership: the profile is authoritative (manifest allowed_regions/home/backup/kms/egress ? profile.allowed_regions); one fixture set (valid + every RESIDENCY_* error incl. schema/invalid-field/toolchain/profile) yields identical pass/block from core.packaging.validate and cmd/pfresidency; config/residency-policy.json, config/residency-manifest.json and config/residency-profiles/** are registered with owners; warn only downgrades policy violations, never execution failures; a bounded structured event is written to engineering/residency-gate.json/.jsonl with report_version=1.
in_scope: Residency manifest section in packaging-manifest.json (explicit home_region; IN template).
Standalone Go validator + CLI, stable codes, warn-first then block.
Build/deploy gate + precheck wiring; conformance tests; profile ownership registration.
out_of_scope: A new API route (the existing /packaging/manifest exposes it).
approach: Extend core/packaging.build/validate with an embedded residency section sourced from config/residency-manifest.json (template) or products/<project>/residency-manifest.json (override) + config/residency-profiles/<home>.json. Add go/residencymanifest (Manifest/Policy/Validate + cmd/pfresidency) with fail-closed home/region/backup/KMS/egress/retention checks, stable error codes and block/warn modes. Add docs/RESIDENCY-MANIFEST-GATE.md; tests in Go + test-framework.

EDP-11/BI-PF-1303: RegionCell attestations + PolicyEvaluator decide cross-border transfers; the registry owns policies, the evaluator owns decisions (fail-closed).
EDP-16/BI-PF-1308: retention/lifecycle and object reconciliation; the residency manifest's retention/backup fields must align with it, not duplicate enforcement.
EDP-02/BI-PF-1294 + packaging: core/packaging.py owns packaging-manifest.json; extend it, do not create a second manifest store.
Language rule: new shipped logic -> Go; editing shipped Python is allowed.
existing_path: config/residency-profiles/in-v1.json (IN, restricted, allowed IN) and us-v1.json (US, conditioned, allowed US); config/residency-policy.json {cells:{},default:local}.
go/edpsvc/internal/residency: Policy/PolicyEvaluator/RegionCell/RegionResolver; internal, not importable by a standalone gate.

assumptions: home_region is REQUIRED per product; there is no silent US default. The shipped template config/residency-manifest.json uses IN (in-v1).
Default data classes: product_metadata, generated_source, build_evidence (no tenant PII by default).
Default retention is 365 days; backup daily; KMS provider local/IN rotation 90d; egress empty (no cross-border subprocessors).
The gate defaults to warn for the first release, then block; warn is audited in the JSON report and a stderr line.
The manifest is an embedded residency section in packaging-manifest.json; config/residency-manifest.json is the default/template, and products/<project>/residency-manifest.json overrides it.
A standalone Go module is used for the gate because go/edpsvc/internal/residency is internal and the gate must run at packaging/deploy without edpsvc.
divergences: Prior proposal defaulted home_region to US; replaced by explicit-required with an IN template after operator review.
The stale analysis suggested gate/residency_check.go and extending run_manifest.py; the current owner is core/packaging.py and go/residencymanifest.
A second Go residency type set exists (internal edpsvc vs standalone gate); the gate is deliberately standalone and reuses the policy files, not the internal package.

impact_review.evidence: No new HTTP surface: the existing GET /packaging/manifest exposes the embedded residency section; a build/deploy CLI validates it.
4 detailed ACs incl. explicit home_region (template IN), stable error codes, backup/KMS rules, manifest override/precedence, warn stderr, neutral doc name, and fail-closed unknown/missing home.
New validator/CLI in Go (go/residencymanifest); Python edits to core/packaging.py + a tooling gate script; language_rule_review BI-PF-1304 = OK.
Reuses config/residency-profiles policies and core/packaging.py's manifest instead of a new store; the internal evaluator is not imported (internal).
Manifest is product-level metadata (no tenant rows); allowed/backup/kms/egress regions are validated against the home policy; no cross-border egress by default.
Retention/backup are declared and checked for policy bounds; enforcement remains EDP-16/lifecycle.
Packaging build/validate + a precheck gate; block is configurable to warn; rollback is a revert; no schema/data change.

risks: home_region is explicit; a product with no manifest now fails closed (intentional). The shipped template uses IN and products can override.
The standalone Go types duplicate the internal edpsvc residency types; a conformance test + schema_version guard the file contract.
Warn-first rollout: the first release warns; block follows after products have manifests.
rollback: Set config/residency-policy.json gate_mode=warn or revert the commit; manifests remain informational.
evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=0630271075c3
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - **Type duplication between `go/residencymanifest` and internal `edpsvc` residency types creates two sources of truth.** When the service model evolves (e.g., new region, added field), the standalone Go types will silently drift — the gate will pass manifests the service rejects, or worse, reject valid ones. Either share a single schema (JSON Schema + codegen), or add a schema-fingerprint test that fails CI when the two diverge.
  - **No phased rollout strategy.** The AC says `gate_mode` defaults to `block`. Any product that has not yet populated `config/residency-manifest.json` will have its builds stopped on the first commit that ships this gate. The design should specify an explicit two-step rollout: (1) ship manifest with warn mode + a tracking issue per product, (2) flip to block after all products pass. The rollback note ("set gate_mode=warn") is a reactive escape hatch, not a rollout plan.
  - **Gate crash / validator-binary-missing behaviour is unspecified.** If `cmd/pfresidency` fails to compile, is absent from `PATH`, or exits non-zero for a non-validation reason (e.g., JSON parse error in the profile), the gate must treat this as **block** (fail-closed). The design only says "blocks (exit 1) or warns per gate_mode" — clarify that any non-zero exit not attributable to a known validation error code is always a block regardless of `gate_mode`.
MINOR:
  - **No aggregate observability on validation failure rates.** A JSON report per run is good for individual diagnosis, but there is no metric, log line, or structured event that a monitoring system can consume to answer "how many products are currently non-compliant?" at fleet scale. Add a minimum signal (e.g., a structured log to a known stream or a counter file).
  - **Error-code stability contract is stated but not defined.** The AC says "stable error codes" — the design should enumerate the codes, assign them to a namespace (e.g., `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME`, `RESIDENCY_HOME_NOT_ALLOWED`), and state that any addition or removal is a versioned contract change.
  - **Backup/KMS sub-field validation rules are incomplete.** The AC lists `backup.encrypted`, `backup.frequency`, `kms.rotation_days` but the validation rules section only covers region subsets and `retention.days`. Add explicit rules: `backup.encrypted` must be `true`, `kms.rotation_days > 0`, and `backup.frequency` must be a recognised value.
  - **`config/residency-manifest.json` as a static file vs. per-product dynamic generation.** The design says "sourced from `config/residency-manifest.json`" — clarify whether this file is a template, a single-product default, or a per-product override mechanism. If multi-product, the file path convention needs to be stated.
NIT:
  - `--report` writes to a file or stdout but is non-fatal; consider also emitting a one-line summary to stderr when validation fails in warn mode so operators do not miss it.
  - The `docs/EDP-RESIDENCY-MANIFEST.md` filename is product-specific; if the manifest becomes multi-product, a more neutral name (e.g., `docs/RESIDENCY-MANIFEST-GATE.md`) reduces confusion.
SUMMARY:
  - The design correctly identifies fail-closed validation, a Go-first validator, and a clear block/warn mode as the right pattern. The two highest risks are: (1) type duplication between the standalone Go module and the internal service types, which will drift without a schema-fingerprint or codegen strategy, and (2) the absence of a phased rollout plan that avoids blocking all builds on day one. Address the gate-crash fail-closed rule and the minimum observability signal before Gate 1.5.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
